reply:
Dear Alberto, all, 
Thanks for the discussion during the official offline. At the end of offline session, there was a saying that the Technique 1 part is almost stable. Sorry but there is still one issue that is not clarified or solved from our perspective. 
The bullet e) under technique 1 is still not very clear to us. 
For the bullet e), it seems should be “by adding a term equal to the two-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN” instead of one-way Doppler. 
First, the logic for the Doppler frequency compensation of Rel-20 UE should be same and aligned with bullet d) the time domain compensation behavior. Since two-way propagation delay (RTT) is compensated in the time domain, then it should be same for the Doppler shift/frequency domain to compensate the two-way frequency offsets. 
For the bullet d), the DL reference time is the DL reception time at UE. Then the Rel-17 UL timing compensation is the RTT (two-way propagation delay). Then if the frequency domain follows the same logic, then the DL reference frequency is the carrier frequency of the DL reception ( = nominal DL frequency – Doppler shifts in DL). The Rel-17 UE behavior for UL compensation is to compensate the two-way Doppler shifts based on the DL (actual) reception carrier frequency. Then the item e) should be “by adding a term of the two-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN”, i.e. with the Rel-17 UL compensation in frequency domain minus the two-way UL Doppler between the CRP and the SAN. At last, it seems that the Rel-20 UE does not compensate anything in the UL carrier frequency in general, which is similar to the behavior of unmodified UE. The marginal compensation in UL frequency domain is the difference between the actual one-way Doppler shift and the one between CRP and the SAN. 
Based on the illustration in Figure 2 in R1-2610456, “by adding a term equal to the one-way UL Doppler between the CRP and the SAN” is only correct in the condition that the reference frequency is nominal UL carrier frequency. Based on this assumption, the Rel-17 UE behavior is to compensate the UL transmission with one-way Doppler, which is different from the description of the case that DL reception frequency is considered as reference. Though it is the same fact and behavior, but with difference reference frequency assumptions, there would be a one-way Doppler compensation and two-way Doppler compensation. 
Two options can be considered to further clarify this issue. 
Option 1: 
e.	The UE uplink frequency pre-compensation is modified (with respect to the current one as defined by uplinkPrecompensation-r17) by adding a term equal to the one-way  two-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN, when actual DL reception carrier frequency is considered as the reference frequency for UL compensation.
Option 2: 
e.	The UE uplink frequency pre-compensation is modified (with respect to the current one as defined by uplinkPrecompensation-r17) by adding a term equal to the one-way uplink Doppler between the CRP and the SAN, when the nominal UL carrier frequency is considered as the reference frequency for UL compensation.
Nominal UL carrier frequency is the one that UE determined based on the DL actual reception frequency and estimated DL Doppler shifts based on the UE location and ephemeris information. 
Either option 1 or option 2 can clarify the background and the assumptions of one-way or two-way Doppler shift compensation. Hope this can clarify the issue and smooth the online discussion. 
Best Regards
YI ZHENG
CMCC
